title: Cottage Pie
subtitle: Beef mince filling under a mashed potato crust
excerpt: Beef mince braised with onion, carrot, celery, and beef stock, finished with Worcestershire sauce, topped with fluffy mashed potato, and baked until crisp and golden.

recipe.sourceNotes: Cottage pie predates shepherd's pie in print, first appearing in 1791 as a way for rural labourers (who lived in cottages) to use leftover meat from the Sunday joint by mincing it and topping it with the potato that was then becoming affordable as a staple crop. Today cottage pie is made from fresh beef mince. The distinction from shepherd's pie is the meat: beef for cottage pie, lamb for shepherd's. Both are quintessentially British, and both have become weekend staples.

recipeTools.notes: A 28 x 20 cm oven-proof dish for baking.

content.text: Use beef mince with a moderate fat content (10 to 15 per cent) for the best flavour. Too lean and the filling will be dry; too fatty and the sauce will be greasy. Cook the filling long enough that the liquid reduces to a thick, glossy sauce rather than a watery one: a wet filling will make the potato topping collapse.
Heat the oil in a large heavy-based pan. Brown the beef mince in two batches over high heat. Remove and set aside.
In the same pan, soften the onion, carrot, and celery over medium heat for 10 minutes. Add the garlic and tomato paste. Cook for 1 minute. Return the beef.
Add the Worcestershire sauce, stock, thyme, and bay leaves. Season. Simmer uncovered for 25 to 30 minutes until the sauce is thick. Discard the herb sprigs and bay leaves.
Boil the potatoes in salted water until tender, about 20 minutes. Drain and mash with the butter and warm milk until smooth. Season well.
Heat the oven to 200 C / fan 180 C / gas 6. Spoon the filling into a baking dish. Spread the mash over the top and rough the surface with a fork. Bake for 25 to 30 minutes until golden and bubbling.
